# MCP servers

Where these methods are:

- `session.mcp` — `Session.mcp`, a `SessionMcp`

Every method here is generated from igni-core's RPC contract; its documentation is igni's own. The examples run inside an `async` function with `igni` an open `IgniClient` and `session` one of its sessions ([Quick start](/docs/sdk/igni-client/quick-start)).

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`session.mcp.connect()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-connect) | Connect one configured MCP server to this session. |
| [`session.mcp.disconnect()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-disconnect) | Disconnect one MCP server from this session. |
| [`session.mcp.ensure()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-ensure) | Connect this session's configured MCP servers, once. |
| [`session.mcp.server_details()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-server-details) | Describe each of this session's MCP servers in full. |
| [`session.mcp.servers()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-servers) | List this session's configured MCP servers, in configuration order. |
| [`session.mcp.set_tool_enabled()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-set-tool-enabled) | Switch one MCP server's tool on or off for this project. |
| [`session.mcp.status()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/mcp#session-mcp-status) | List this session's MCP servers and whether each is connected. |

## session.mcp.connect()

Connect one configured MCP server to this session.

```python
async def connect(self, server_name: str) -> InfoMessage
```

`server_name` is the server's name in the MCP configuration.
Returns an `info` message, sent in place of an `rpc_response`,
once it is connected. Fails with the reason when it did not connect
(not configured, refused by policy, no tools, approval denied); the
reason is also `get_mcp_server_details`'s `error` for it.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server_name` | `str` | required | `server_name` is the server's name in the MCP configuration. |

**Returns** [`InfoMessage`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/events-reference#infomessage).

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `mcp_connect`, scope `session`, area `mcp`; igni answers with `message`.

**Example**

```python
info = await session.mcp.connect("github")
print(info.text)
```

## session.mcp.disconnect()

Disconnect one MCP server from this session.

```python
async def disconnect(self, server_name: str) -> InfoMessage
```

`server_name` is the server's name in the MCP configuration.
Returns an `info` message, sent in place of an `rpc_response`,
whether or not the server was connected.

## session.mcp.ensure()

Connect this session's configured MCP servers, once.

```python
async def ensure(self) -> McpInitResult
```

Takes no arguments. The first call connects every configured server
and rebuilds the agent with their tools; later calls do nothing.
Returns the servers `connected`, the ones that `failed` with
their errors, whether the agent was `rebuilt`, and, when nothing
was done, `skipped_reason` (`already_initialized`,
`no_configured_servers`, `no_clients_connected`).

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** [`McpInitResult`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#mcpinitresult).

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `ensure_mcp`, scope `session`, area `mcp`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
ready = await session.mcp.ensure()
print("connected:", ready.connected, "failed:", ready.failed)
```

## session.mcp.server_details()

Describe each of this session's MCP servers in full.

```python
async def server_details(self) -> list[McpServerSnapshot]
```

Takes no arguments. Returns one row per server: whether it is
connected, its transport, its tools (names, descriptions, the ones
switched off), its resources and prompts, the last error connecting
it, and whether policy blocks it. Each server is asked in turn, so
a slow one slows the answer.

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** `list[`[`McpServerSnapshot`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#mcpserversnapshot)`]`.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `get_mcp_server_details`, scope `session`, area `mcp`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
for mcp_server_snapshot in await session.mcp.server_details():
    print(mcp_server_snapshot.name, mcp_server_snapshot.connected)
```

## session.mcp.set_tool_enabled()

Switch one MCP server's tool on or off for this project.

```python
async def set_tool_enabled(self, *, enabled: bool, server: str, tool: str) -> McpToolToggleResult
```

`server` and `tool` name the tool; `enabled` is its new state.
The choice is saved in the project's `.igni/mcp-tool-state.json`.
Returns the `server`, `tool` and `enabled` as recorded; the
server and tool are not checked to exist. Fails when the state file
cannot be written.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `bool` | required | `enabled` is its new state. |
| `server` | `str` | required | `server` and `tool` name the tool; |
| `tool` | `str` | required | `server` and `tool` name the tool; |

**Returns** [`McpToolToggleResult`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#mcptooltoggleresult).

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `set_mcp_tool_enabled`, scope `session`, area `mcp`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
toggled = await session.mcp.set_tool_enabled(server="github", tool="delete_repo", enabled=False)
print(toggled.tool, toggled.enabled)
```
